page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Lattice enthalpy of an ionic compound: the
enthalpy change when one mole of the solid
steps.why: Separating oppositely charged ions needs energy, so in this dissociation form the lattice enthalpy is positive. Some books define it for lattice formation instead; the same number then carries a negative sign.
common_mistakes: Writing ions in solution instead of ions in the gaseous state — dissolving in water is a different process.
Dropping one mole from the definition.
steps.memory_tip: Lattice enthalpy takes the crystal apart completely: one mole of solid to separate gaseous ions.
steps.margin_note: Gaseous state and one mole are the two checked phrases.

steps.label: The example

lines.text: One mole of ionic solid → separate gaseous ions

steps.why: NaCl is the standard example; the large positive value shows how strongly the ions attract each other in the crystal.
common_mistakes: Writing the value with a negative sign while using the dissociation definition — breaking the lattice absorbs energy.
steps.memory_tip: NaCl and +788 kJ mol⁻¹: a large positive number, because the crystal must be pulled apart into gaseous ions.
steps.margin_note: The sign must match the definition used: dissociation gives plus.

insider_note: The two-word phrase gaseous state is the whole question — answers that end at dissociates into its ions lose the definition mark.
